The tags of every package zone containing the target: distinct, sorted, space-separated; empty outside every zone. Test with contains.
How many package zones contain the target.
SPEC-171's five ownership states for a mobile on the surface: 0 non-concerned, 1 pending, 2 transferred in, 3 assumed, 4 transferred out. Derived from the attention state and the ownership fields.
Callsign of the position responsible for the mobile, SPEC-171's responsible Controller; blank when nobody holds it.

Where the mobile is in its movement, from the zones, speed, ground flag and height: 0 unknown, 1 on stand, 2 pushback, 3 taxiing, 4 holding, 5 on runway, 6 taking off, 7 departed, 8 airborne, 9 approaching, 10 landed. Thresholds and zone tags are policy.json surface.movement.

Runway incursion alert stage from runway monitoring: 0 none, 1 Stage One (a caution; colour the label background), 2 Stage Two (the flashing alert). 0 for every mobile while policy.json runwayMonitoring is absent.

Why the RIMCAS stage: 0 none, 1 two on the runway, 2 two on the runway and closing, 3 arrival approaching an occupied runway, 4 arrival imminent on an occupied runway, 5 closed runway, 6 opposite direction (two moving head-on), 7 restricted area (inside a zone tagged strip.restrictedZoneTag; rimcasRunway is blank).
The monitored runway the mobile is on or approaching, as airport and pair (EGLL 09L/27R); blank for none.
Seconds until an approaching mobile reaches the runway strip; -1 for a mobile not approaching one.
The Impending Arrival Window row the approach sits in, one of runwayMonitoring.arrival.countdownS (the LVP set in low visibility); -1 for none. Group a list by it for the window.
1 while low visibility procedures are in force for runway monitoring, else 0.

The highest-priority safety net alert standing on this aircraft: 0 none, 1 BUST, 2 CLAM, 3 RAM, 4 MSAW, 5 APW, 6 AIW, 7 hold intrusion, 8 MTCD, 9 TCT, 10 RIMCAS, 11 STCA, 12 AFDAS, 13 emergency squawk. The order is policy.json safetyNets.priority.

Severity of that alert: 0 none, 1 info, 2 warning, 3 alert. RIMCAS Stage One is a warning and Stage Two an alert, so [">=", "alertSeverity", "2"] on a text item is the flashing ALERT row every net shares.
That alert's own text, the server's wording for a server net and the evaluator's for a client one; blank for none.
The second aircraft of a pairwise alert (MTCD, TCT, STCA); blank otherwise.
How many alerts stand on this aircraft, after the system's safetyNets.show filter.
1 while the controller has acknowledged the highest alert (the acknowledgeAlert action); a change of kind or severity clears it. Gate a blink on it and leave the colour alone.
1 while safety net sounds are silenced for this session (the muteAlerts action). The same for every aircraft, so a list header can show it.
STCA severity on this aircraft: 0 none, 1 info, 2 warning, 3 alert. 0 while the system hides the kind or nothing runs it.
MSAW severity on this aircraft: 0 none, 1 info, 2 warning, 3 alert. 0 while the system hides the kind or the server does not run it.

3 while this aircraft squawks 7500, 7600 or 7700, else 0. alertText names the condition; policy.json safetyNets.emergencySquawk turns the net off.

The minimum safe altitude the package's msaw.geojson surface has under this aircraft, in feet AMSL; 0 where it has none and 0 when the package ships no surface. The MSAW net measures the aircraft against this, and a label can show it, which TopSky cannot. Overlap is resolved as TopSky reads its file: the lowest order wins.
